tags.gist: Wants practical modifiers added: reversibility, time to correction, error detectability, version traceability, safeguard independence, exposure before containment and workflow stability.
Wants directiveness judged by observed behavior, since personalization, urgency, defaults, confidence display and tool use can turn information into direction.
Wants multi-turn evaluation to cover context accumulation or loss, escalation, refusal, interruption and safe stop.
Wants claim-specific, traceable evidence naming population, setting, reference standard, criteria and exclusions, with adversarial, shifted and repeated-run testing.
Would not presume public benchmarks predict clinical performance, and wants external adjudication, preregistration or locked tests where sponsors control testing.
Limits synthetic data to schema tests, fault injection and specified rare cases, keeping its results apart from real data unless both estimate one quantity.
Says monitoring should add to rather than replace premarket evidence, accepting more uncertainty only when failures are detectable, limited, bounded and containable.
Wants a versioned baseline, indicators, investigation thresholds, review ownership and rollback rules, with reassessment after any material change or new signal.
Wants a versioned dependency inventory with change notice, pinning, regression and canary tests, and narrower permitted use when a dependency cannot be controlled.
Wants action-sequence criteria covering tool selection, authorization, least privilege, approval before irreversible acts, interruption and rollback, with oversight before action.
Sums up asks for structured modifiers, traceable evidence, explicit uncertainty and versioned records, with null and adverse evidence kept visible.
